subject: redPanda
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: red panda balancing on a mossy stone.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a stylized red panda model sitting on a mossy stone, using a toon/cel-shading kit with anime-style eyes and fur edges, aiming to keep the module efficient yet visually rich while sketching proportions for the body, tail, and scale.

I'm working out the stone base as a faceted boulder with moss shading, then setting up the panda's skeleton joints -- hips, chest, and a spine chain built from a curved path -- to establish the pose standing on the rock with one paw lifted for balance.

I'm checking whether to pass the chain point or its vector when positioning the head joint, then sketching the body sweep along the spine chain with an elliptical radius profile sized for a chunkier chest.

For coloring I'm using a countershading approach on the fur edge, orange cel on top and dark brown below to match a red panda's coat, then moving to leg placement with hip and foot targets and two-segment limb lengths for the hind legs.

Setting up the leg chains with hip, knee, and ankle joints parented to the hips, then sweeping the geometry with a small radius for the leg thickness before adding paw shapes.

For the raised right paw, I'm positioning it forward and slightly up like a wave gesture, computing the bend direction so the elbow angles downward and the limb plane works out geometrically given the shoulder and target positions.

Now moving to the head design: shaping a wide head sphere with scaled dimensions, and planning red panda facial markings — white-rimmed ears, cream muzzle, dark tear marks running from the eyes, and anime-style eyes with amber iris decals placed relative to the head's local coordinate space so cheek and muzzle coloring align correctly regardless of world position.

Working out the head paint logic — cream coloring applied to the muzzle and cheek tuft zones based on distance from head center, then wrapped in a cel shader so lighting splits into lit and shadow tones. I'm also positioning the head along the neck's upward-forward curve, placing the head joint center a bit above and forward of the spine and neck midpoints.

Setting up the snout and jaw geometry now — a cream muzzle sphere with a dark nose tip, plus a separate jaw joint parented to the head so the lower jaw can move independently, sized as a small flattened sphere positioned just below and forward of the head center.

Now working on the ears, aiming for the rounded, oversized look of a real red panda with lighter inner fur — flattened spheres positioned near the top of the head and scaled asymmetrically to get that triangular, cupped shape.

Now I'm working out eye placement as decals on the skull surface, sizing them small and positioning via hit azimuth/elevation. I'm also adding tear-mark stripes below each eye using dark brown decals running from eye to mouth, then setting up mirroring so the left and right sides match.

I'm sketching cream eyebrow spots, cheap whisker rods along the muzzle, and now building the bushy tail as a chained path curving upward behind the hips for balance.

For the tail's coloring, I'm working out alternating ring stripes using the sweep parameter, mapping position along the tail to alternating dark red and orange bands with a toon-style cel shading wrapper, darkening toward the tip.

I'm also considering adding a Genshin-style decorative touch, like a small glowing elemental accent or tassel, to give it more character flair.

I'll finalize the set of embellishments: a collar with a golden bell and red ribbon, glowing dendro crystals or mushrooms on the stone, moss, small flowers, and a few floating glowing "seelie" particle orbs for atmosphere. I'm also planning the base elements, like smaller stones and grass tufts, along with the handful of SVG textures needed (eye, grass blade, tear mark, petals) and starting to sketch the collar geometry around the neck.

For the ribbon tails, I'll just use simple rods extending down from the bell hit point rather than full bezier sweeps. For the moss, I'm planning to add custom paint on the stone where the surface normal points upward, giving it a mottled grey-blue cel look, then scattering small moss tuft cards on top wherever the normal is strongly vertical.

I need to filter grass/moss cards so they don't poke through the panda's paws -- excluding any near the footprint box close to center while keeping the stone's outer edges free. For the stone lathe shape, I'm sketching a profile with the top at y=0.2 and radius up to 0.42, making sure the panda's feet sit just above that top surface.

Shifting the stone's center slightly (z=0.02) so it better covers the panda's footprint span, including hind paws and tail, while keeping the lathe outline a simple sharp-faceted polygon rather than a smoothed curve.

For the stone paint function, I'm blending moss and stone colors based on height and noise: moss where the normal faces upward (mossy top) mixed between light/dark moss tones, stone color mixed between light/dark stone tones elsewhere, with a smoothstep transition driven by noise-perturbed normal.y, plus a cheap lighting multiply using n.y.

I'm wrapping it with cel shading so shadows derive properly for the Genshin style look. I'm also adding a couple small boulder shapes using flat icosahedron geometry with stone paint, placed beside the main stone, plus glowing dendro crystal clusters (low-poly cones) and floating seed orbs with teal-green glow near the stone, and a glowing flower center.

Now I'm working out the cheek fur tufts using small flattened cone spikes pointing outward-back from the head bone, colored cream with cel shading. Writing fur edge shader logic...

For legs I'm using a dark brown cel color, skipping paw pads and claw details to keep things simple, and adding a dark nose sphere at the snout tip plus tear lines near the eyes while skipping the mouth line and ink outline since those aren't feasible for this rig.

Now I'm working out the skeleton structure—attaching the leg chain to a spine joint, building the spine as a catmull-rom curve with three joints parented to the hips, and starting on the neck chain extending from the spine's end point.

I'm figuring out the body's vertical layout: setting a baseline y, computing belly radius clearance over leg length, and spacing the spine's control points along the z-axis with slight y rises toward the head.

Now I'm defining the taper function for the body cross-section radii, using a sine-based curve so the belly bulges in the middle, then laying out the neck control points and head center position so they connect smoothly to the spine.

Setting up the hind leg with hip and foot positions, checking bend lengths and distances work out properly, and giving the thigh and shin chunkier sweep radii for a sturdier look.

For the paw, I'm planning a scaled sphere at the foot position with a slight forward offset and dark coloring, and considering adding small toe-nub spheres via a simple loop or helper function to give it some texture without overcomplicating things.

Now I'm working out the raised front leg: placing the shoulder joint near the body, aiming the chain toward a paw position close to the head, checking the elbow bend direction and verifying the segment lengths match the distance between shoulder and target. Then I'm setting up the standing left front leg similarly, with its own shoulder and foot coordinates and bend direction.

I'm adding scattered grass tufts as small card sprites on top of the stone, oriented to face upward with some lean and random variation, followed by placing a small flower stem near the stone's edge.

Placing crystal positions near the stone top, computing cone centers from base and lean direction, then adding a few small floating glow orbs scattered around as sparkle accents, skipping leaves and lanterns for now.

I'm scattering mossy icosahedron clumps onto the stone using the stick helper for placement, and sketching a small offset helper to position objects along normalized directions for consistent spacing.

Now I'm pulling in the builder's core utilities and toon/glow kits, then shaping the skull as a scaled sphere part attached to the head bone, making sure the head-center constant is defined before use so the muzzle sphere can reference it too.

Positioning the muzzle, nose, and cream cel-shaded color, then working out ear placement with a forward-tilted direction vector and cylinder geometry for layered ear shapes.

Now I'm sketching the eye decal placement using a hit-test fallback, and designing the tear mark as a tapered SVG path in dark brown, positioned via azimuth and elevation offsets near the eye.

I'm adjusting lift heights to avoid z-fighting between the tear and eye decals, skipping forehead markings since red pandas don't have cream brows here, then starting on thin whisker rods extending from the muzzle using a low-poly cylinder.

Now I'm placing a red ribbon loop around the neck tube and figuring out where a bell should attach — casting a ray from the neck center at a downward-forward angle to find the surface hit point, then adding a gold bell sphere with a small ring embedded into it.

Shaping the tail with a swept radius profile that tapers and darkens near the tip, then moving on to body fur coloring by height and checking the head joint setup.

Now placing the jaw joint and verifying the stone base sits flat on the ground, then positioning small rocks around it with offsets to avoid overlapping the stone's radius.

I'm adding floating glow orbs with soft green tint at a few positions above the scene, and planning the surface scatter logic for the stone's skin with a filter that avoids certain regions based on height and position.

Now I'm setting up moss lump scatter with a similar but wider edge filter that excludes the panda's area, and sketching grass blade SVGs using layered green paths to create a tufted look.

For the flower SVG, I'm adding a stem rectangle with five petal circles in white-pink around a yellow center, then finalizing the orange cel-shading color with an automatic shadow tone before writing out the complete piece.
